title: Cognitive Inclusivity in AI Coding Assistants: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
abstract: arXiv:2610.41192v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI coding assistants are commonly used for daily software development tasks. While prior research has examined their impact on productivity and code quality, less is understood about how these tools support diverse ways of thinking. Evidence from non-AI software engineering tools suggests that mismatches between tool design and users' cognitive styles can introduce inclusivity barriers, but it remains unclear whether similar issues arise in AI coding assistants. We investigate how developers with different cognitive styles experience and interact with these tools and whether they exhibit cognitive inclusivity challenges. We conducted a controlled laboratory study with 20 student participants using GitHub Copilot to complete code generation, debugging, and refactoring tasks. translated_title: AI编程助手中的认知包容性：来自GitHub Copilot的证据
translated_abstract: AI编程助手被广泛用于日常软件开发任务。尽管已有研究考察了它们对生产力和代码质量的影响，但人们对这些工具如何支持多样化的思维方式仍知之甚少。来自非AI软件工程工具的证据表明，工具设计与用户认知风格之间的不匹配可能带来包容性障碍，但目前尚不清楚AI编程助手是否也存在类似问题。我们研究了具有不同认知风格的开发者如何体验和使用这些工具，以及他们是否表现出认知包容性方面的挑战。我们开展了一项受控实验室研究，邀请20名学生参与者使用GitHub Copilot完成代码生成、调试和重构任务。通过出声思维协议、半结构化访谈和归纳式主题分析，我们识别了用户交互中的模式。随后，我们应用GenderMag框架……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过让20名学生使用GitHub Copilot完成代码生成、调试和重构任务的受控实验室实验，揭示了具有不同认知风格的开发者在使用AI编程助手时可能面临的认知包容性挑战。
en_tdlr: Through a controlled laboratory study with 20 students using GitHub Copilot for code generation, debugging, and refactoring tasks, this paper reveals cognitive inclusivity challenges faced by developers with different cognitive styles when using AI coding assistants.
